# Examples

Each example is one code change, run through a formal verifier, with the verdict and why it matters.
Together they show what verification catches that code review and tests miss, and what it lets through.

All examples so far use [behavioural contracts](tools/contracts/README.md) (approach B8 in [`approaches.md`](approaches.md)) on the order state machine of [Box Office](apps/boxoffice/README.md), the demo ticketing system.
The principle is that the contract may change only where the developer intends a change.

<!-- examples:begin (generated by examples/tools/build.py) -->
| # | Example | Verdict | Existing tests | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 001 | [A switch cleanup that keeps the money for declined orders](001-merged-case-keeps-money/README.md) | ✗ Violation: 2 of 36 cases changed | caught | functional | high | cleanup |
| 002 | [A refactor believed equivalent that changes null handling](002-equality-refactor-changes-null-handling/README.md) | ✗ Violation: 1 of 36 cases changed | **missed** | functional, compatibility | medium | refactor |
| 003 | [Logging a timestamp makes the decision unverifiable](003-timestamp-makes-decision-nondeterministic/README.md) | ⚠ Unverifiable | **missed** | determinism | medium | logging |
| 004 | [An equivalent refactor passes without touching the contract](004-equivalent-refactor-passes/README.md) | ✓ Verified: all 36 cases match | pass | no-false-positive | none | refactor |
| 005 | [An intended change, reviewed as a one-line contract diff](005-intended-change-reviewed-as-contract-diff/README.md) | ✓ Verified: all 36 cases match | pass | functional | none | feature |
<!-- examples:end -->

The *Existing tests* column is measured, not claimed: the generator runs the module's unit tests against each patch. A **missed** entry means the tests pass and the change would have shipped.

**Verdicts:**
- **✗ Violation:** behaviour changed, but the developer did not intend it. The build fails, with a concrete input for each changed case.
- **✓ Verified:** the code behaves exactly as its contract says, for every possible input.
  An intended change passes once its contract is regenerated, and the contract diff is what the reviewer approves.
- **⚠ Unverifiable:** the verifier refuses to give a verdict, for example because the code is no longer provably pure. The build fails, because "we could not check" must not read as "fine".

## How to read an example

Each example's page has the same sections:

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| Summary table | Verdict, categories, severity if the change shipped unnoticed, what kind of change it was, the verified unit, the approach |
| The change | What the developer meant to do, the code before and after, and the patch |
| What the verifier found | The counterexamples (inputs whose outcome changed), the reason for refusing, or the contract diff |
| Would the existing tests have caught it? | The module's unit tests, run against the same patch: the baseline the verifier is compared with |
| Why it matters | The production risk |
| Why the verdict is right | How the verifier reached it, and why it is a proof and not a sample |
| What to do | The resolution |
| Evidence | The verifier's console output and SARIF report, unedited, and the JDK APIs the proof trusted |

## Layout

```
examples/
  README.md                  this page; the table above is generated
  index.json                 the same list, for tools (generated)
  NNN-short-name/
    example.json             written by hand: the change, its risk, the expected verdict, the explanation
    change.patch             written by hand: a unified diff against the repo
    result.json              generated: verdict, counterexamples, before and after excerpts, contract diff
    result.sarif             generated: the verifier's SARIF report
    verifier-output.txt      generated: the verifier's console output
    README.md                generated: the page you read
  schema/
    example.schema.json      the format of example.json
    result.schema.json       the format of result.json
  approaches.md              the verification approaches by level, and the plan for the demos
  apps/boxoffice/            the subject system the examples change
  tools/contracts/           the verifier: behavioural contracts
  tools/build.py             the generator: runs every example and writes the generated files
  setup/                     the toolchain installer
```

Everything the verifier says is generated by running it, so no example can claim a result the tool did not produce.
The generator also fails when a verdict differs from the example's `expected.verdict`, so the examples double as regression tests of the verifier.

## Run or add an example

```bash
python3 examples/tools/build.py          # run every example, then rewrite the pages and the table
python3 examples/tools/build.py 002      # run one
```

It needs Java 25 (no Docker). Each example takes a few seconds: the patch is applied to a temporary copy of the repo, which is then compiled and verified.

To add an example:

1. Make the change in your working copy, and save it with `jj diff --git > examples/NNN-short-name/change.patch`. Then undo the change.
2. Write `examples/NNN-short-name/example.json`, following [`schema/example.schema.json`](schema/example.schema.json). An editor that understands JSON Schema will complete and check the fields.
3. Run `python3 examples/tools/build.py NNN`, and read the generated page.
